headline: Ghana Plans to Stop Exporting Raw Minerals by 2030
meta_description: Ghana aims to end unprocessed mineral exports by 2030, keeping more wealth at home through local processing and manufacturing.
summary_short: Ghana targets an end to raw mineral exports by 2030, shifting toward domestic processing to create jobs and industrial growth.
body:
Ghana has set an ambitious goal to stop exporting unprocessed mineral ores by 2030, a move designed to transform the country's mineral wealth into local jobs, manufacturing, and industrial capacity. President John Dramani Mahama announced the target at the African Minerals Policy Forum in Accra, framing the shift as essential to Africa's economic sovereignty. For decades, Ghana has watched manganese and bauxite leave its ports as raw materials, only to import the finished products back—a pattern that has cost the country skilled employment, technological advancement, and genuine economic growth. Through legal measures and clear timelines, the government plans a phased prohibition on raw ore exports, redirecting minerals instead toward in-country processing in bauxite-to-aluminum production, iron ore and steel, manganese processing, and gold refining.

The ambition extends beyond Ghana's borders. Mahama called for African countries to cooperate rather than compete, building regional value chains where minerals mined in one nation could be processed in another and supplied to manufacturers across the continent. Such collaboration, he argued, would strengthen the continent's industrial capacity and allow countries to capture greater value from their own resources.

Ghana has already begun moving this vision forward. In April 2025, parliament established GoldBod, a statutory authority with exclusive rights to buy and export gold and precious minerals. By October, GoldBod had refined locally 5.4 metric tons of the 5.7 metric tons it purchased from artisanal and small-scale mining operations—nearly 95% refinement locally. The government is also refining 30% of large-scale mining output under the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Program. Mahama emphasized that mineral development cannot be deemed successful if mining communities are left with polluted rivers, damaged farmland, and few lasting benefits. The Accra Reset agenda represents both an economic strategy and a commitment to ensuring that Ghana's mineral wealth truly benefits its people.
quick_facts: Ghana targets complete end to raw mineral exports by 2030
GoldBod refined 95% of gold locally in October 2025
President Mahama announced goal at African Minerals Policy Forum in Accra
Plan includes bauxite, manganese, iron ore, and gold processing
Regional cooperation proposed for African continental value chains
